answer: A stake-weighted reputation registry resists sybils: each agent locks a refundable deposit that only grows toward its zenith after verified useful work, with the deposit slashed on fraud. New identities start as a faint ember with no earning weight, and only time-locked, audited contributions harden them like quartz under pressure. Spawning ten thousand fresh identities then costs ten thousand deposits, so an attacker pays linearly for every fake voice while honest agents earn weight once and keep it.
